title: Smart Multiplication
summary: Multiply fast by numbers near a power of ten: $\times 9 = \times 10 - \times 1$, $\times 99 = \times 100 - \times 1$, $\times 999 = \times 1000 - \times 1$. Spot the digit patterns of $\times 11$, $\times 101$ and $\times 1001$, and see why they work.
bigIdeas: Numbers like $9$, $99$ and $999$ are one less than $10$, $100$ and $1000$: multiply by the round number, then take one lot away.
Numbers like $11$, $101$ and $1001$ are a round number plus one: they make the digits repeat or add.
tips: $\times 11$ for two digits: split them and put their sum in the middle: $43 \times 11 = 473$.
If the middle sum is $10$ or more, carry the $1$: $87 \times 11 = 957$.
